html:
Nagarjuna was a Buddhist monk and philosopher of south India who lived about 150 to 250 CE. He founded the Madhyamaka, or Middle Way, school and is the most important Buddhist thinker after the Buddha himself.

Little about his life is certain. Tradition links him with the Andhra country under the Satavahana kings, and a letter of advice to one of those kings survives under his name. The valley of Nagarjunakonda there is named after him.

His main book is the Mulamadhyamakakarika, "Root Verses on the Middle Way". Its claim is that all things are empty. Nothing exists by its own nature; each thing arises only in dependence on other things. He argues this by taking each idea his rivals held, such as cause, motion, the self and time, and showing that it falls into contradiction if it is treated as fixed. Emptiness is not nothingness, he says, but the middle way between "it exists" and "it does not".

His thought underlies Mahayana Buddhism. It was taught at Nalanda and passed to China, Japan and Tibet, where it is still the core of monastic study.
sum: Nagarjuna was a Buddhist monk and philosopher of south India who lived about 150 to 250 CE. He founded the Madhyamaka, or Middle Way, school and is the most important Buddhist thinker after the Buddha himself.
